about: Research sheet for the Idaho county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Idaho
phones_sentence: Veterans office phones and addresses come from the Idaho Division of Veterans Services’ Office of Veterans Advocacy page. Most counties have no state office; call the Central Support Office or ask your county courthouse about a county veterans service officer.

offices.source_title: Idaho Division of Veterans Services: Office of Veterans Advocacy
offices.note: Office of Veterans Advocacy service officers are accredited and help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and appeals at no charge. There is no state residency requirement for help.
offices.selection: Office address and phones as printed on the division’s Office of Veterans Advocacy page (last updated May 7, 2026); its Service Officers page (last updated May 15, 2026) gives the Boise line for the Mountain Home office. The division publishes no county assignments, so a county without an office shows the division’s statewide card. Bingham County’s veterans page (https://web.binghamid.gov/clerk/veterans.html) says most Idaho counties have a county veterans service officer, so that card also points to the courthouse.

programs.name: Idaho veterans: Office of Veterans Advocacy for claims help
programs.organization: Idaho Division of Veterans Services, Office of Veterans Advocacy
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from the Idaho Division of Veterans Services’ accredited state service officers, in offices in Boise, Caldwell, Mountain Home, Twin Falls, Pocatello, Lewiston and Post Falls.
programs.next_step: Call the office nearest you, or the Central Support Office at 208-780-1300, to make an appointment with a veterans service officer.
constraints: Offices are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; messages can be left 24 hours a day.
Most counties have no state office; many have a county veterans service officer at the courthouse.
programs.phone_label: Idaho Division of Veterans Services Central Support Office (208-780-1300)

programs.name: Idaho Area Agencies on Aging and Aging and Disability Resource Center
programs.organization: Idaho Commission on Aging and the six Area Agencies on Aging
programs.description: Idaho’s six Area Agencies on Aging, coordinated by the Idaho Commission on Aging, are the local starting point for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers: information and assistance, meals, help at home, caregiver support, legal assistance and adult protection. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging, call the Idaho Commission on Aging at 877-471-2777, or dial 2-1-1.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIBA) for Idaho
programs.organization: Idaho Department of Insurance, Senior Health Insurance Benefits Advisors (SHIBA)
programs.description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from Idaho’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, SHIBA: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help with Medicare complaints, in person, by phone or by email.
programs.next_step: Call the SHIBA Medicare Help Line at 800-247-4422 or use the Ask SHIBA form. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: SHIBA does not sell insurance or recommend specific plans. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

programs.name: Idaho Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Idaho Commission on Aging, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
programs.description: Advocacy for residents of skilled nursing and assisted living facilities. Idaho’s local ombudsmen and Adult Protective Services both work through the six Area Agencies on Aging.
programs.next_step: Call the Area Agency on Aging for the county (choose a county above) and ask for the long-term care ombudsman, or call the State Ombudsman at the Idaho Commission on Aging, 877-471-2777. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult, call the same Area Agency on Aging. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.
programs.phone_label: Idaho Commission on Aging, State Ombudsman (877-471-2777)

sources.title: Idaho Commission on Aging: Adult Protective Services

programs.name: Free legal help for Idaho older adults
programs.description: Idaho Legal Aid Services gives free civil legal help to Idahoans 60 and older and to people with low incomes, including a Senior and Public Benefits Legal Advice Line. The Area Agencies on Aging also arrange legal assistance for older adults.
programs.next_step: Call 208-746-7541 for the Legal Advice Lines (phone intake Monday to Wednesday, 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. Mountain Time), or apply online. For questions about a lawyer, the Idaho State Bar is at 208-334-4500.
constraints: Legal aid screens by age, income, assets and case type. It does not handle criminal cases.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Idaho
programs.description: Idaho veterans are served by four VA health care systems: VA Boise (Boise VA Medical Center, 500 West Fort Street; 208-422-1000 or toll-free 866-437-5093); VA Spokane, which serves northern Idaho; VA Walla Walla, whose Lewiston VA Clinic is at 1630 23rd Avenue, Building 2; and VA Salt Lake City, whose clinics include Pocatello.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask an Office of Veterans Advocacy service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.
